items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: he certainly knew me because we had worked together in Luis Russell's orchestra at the Roseland

ctx.x: We played a one-nighter in Little Rock, Arkansas, and then on to Chicago where Kirk had a month engagement at the Grand Terrace which was one of the biggest and best known clubs in the city. One night, Tiny Bradshaw came to the club with a.....

party and sat with his back to the band and didn't speak to anyone in the orchestra. He certainly knew me because we had worked together in Luis Russell's orchestra at the Roseland, and he must have known Andy Kirk. But Tiny had had success as a band leader who played mostly in the Southern States and success had gone to his head.

A few nights later, Duke Ellington came to the club with a party and danced with a woman. As he danced and passed in front of the bandstand, he smiled and nodded at each member of the band as we smiled and spoke to him individually. That was the difference in a great person that is someone and Tiny Bradshaw who was nothing to compare with Duke but thought that he was God Almighty.
